'''''Malus ioensis''''', known as the '''Iowa crab''' or '''prairie crabapple''', is a species of [[crabapple]] tree native to the United States. The most common [[Variety (botany)|variety]], ''M. ioensis'' var. ''ioensis'', is found primarily in the prairie regions of the upper [[Mississippi Valley]]. Another variety, ''M. ioensis'' var. ''texana'', or the '''Texas crabapple''', is found only in a small region of [[central Texas]].<ref name="usda">[https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=MAIO ''Malus ioensis''] at the [[USDA]] [[Natural Resources Conservation Service]]</ref>

The Iowa crab can grow up to 10 meters (35 feet) in height. It bears white or pink flowers in the summer and small apple-like berries in the fall.<ref name="wildflower">[http://www.wildflower.org/plants/result.php?id_plant=MAIO Malus ioensis] at the [[University of Texas at Austin]] Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center</ref>

Various wildlife consume the fruit.<ref>{{cite book|last=Little|first=Elbert L.|title=The Audubon Society Field Guide to North American Trees: Eastern Region|publisher=Knopf|location=New York|year=1980|isbn=0-394-50760-6|page=491}}</ref>
